I'm trying to use enum in place of some inductive type definition when I find some performance issue with it.

  • When there are more than 26 constructors, Lean will report error: "maximum recursion depth has been reached". This can be solved by increasing maxRecDepth option of Lean.
  • When the number of constructorsincrease to more than 50, it causes stack overflow of Lean. This can be solved by increasing the thread stack size of Lean server.

Since these issues don't occur when using inductive, I wonder whether it's possible to optimize enum so that it can work better.

By set_option trace.veil.desugar true I suspect the cause is that the Decidable instance generated for distinct is not tail-recursive, so it stackoverflows when there are too many constructors.

While I think it's possible to workaround it (by making the formula size not quadratic but linear wrt. the number of constructors), could you also describe your scenario on why you would need that many constructors?

@George Pîrlea I guess on the SMT translation side, we might also need to translate distinct into SMT-LIB's DISTINCT to avoid formula size explosion?

could you also describe your scenario on why you would need that many constructors?

Actually I'm specifying the behavior of a C program in Veil, so I use enum to define the set of program counters.

By the way, by setting set_option trace.veil.desugar true I find enum actually defines a inductive type and then prove it's an instance of EnumClass. So I wonder how we will benifit from using enum (instead of inductive). For example, does it provide more information to SMT?

@Yizhou Mao

So I wonder how we will benifit from using enum (instead of inductive). For example, does it provide more information to SMT?

Yes, we use the EnumClass axiomatisation to encode the enum when we send it to SMT because we want to stay in pure uninterpreted first-order logic. For execution, e.g. when doing #model_check, we use the inductive type directly, rather than the axiomatisation.

That said, Lean SMT (the framework we use for interacting with SMT) has recently added support for inductive types (using the SMT theory of datatypes, so we will try to ship that into Veil in the next few months and see how it performs.

@Yizhou Mao There are a few performance issues which are relatively easy to fix, but there's a further issue. Currently we generate a structure representing the enum, with one field per constructor, and Lean is limited to having at most 256 fields per structure.

We can get around this limitation, but it would complicate the implementation quite a bit.

Just to get a sense: do you expect to need more than 256 constructors in your enum? (It's fine if the answer is yes.)
I think currently 256 constructors are enough, but in larger programs there may be more PCs, so in the future we may need more than 256 constructors.

I just pushed a fix to veil-2.0-preview. Now it should be able to handle that many constructors (test case) and translate distinct to DISTINCT in SMT-LIB, although the enum command would cost several seconds to do some internal proof, but that's a separate issue.

I tried Lean-SMT on Lean v4.29 and it seems that proof reconstruction for data type is not supported yet (?), so let's stick with enum for now ...

If in the future you would have more than 256 constructors, then probably you will need to encode them as Fin instead of an inductive type or enum.
@Yizhou Mao I've pushed another commit which should make this faster. You should now be able to use enums with just under 256 constructors with quite reasonable performance.
